## Bio

![](sarayu_image2.jpg){width="350px" style="display: block; margin: 0 auto 1em auto;"}
I’m a marine scientist and environmental communicator interested in the space between research, people, and the stories we tell about the environment. I like bringing different kinds of knowledge and expertise together, making complex information easier to understand, and finding creative ways to turn research into something people can use.

I recently graduated from the Bren School at UC Santa Barbara with a Master of Environmental Science and Management, specializing in coastal resource management and environmental communication. My work spans applied research along the California Current, with an emphasis on science communication and data visualization. I'm interested in using visual storytelling to make environmental data accessible and give agency to the communities and institutions whose story it is telling.

I've been part of long-term monitoring efforts including [ACCESS](https://accessoceans.org/) and [keystone datasets on the Farallon Islands](https://www.pointblue.org/our-work/keystone-datasets/). My field experience includes one season as a preventative search and rescue volunteer in Hetch-Hetchy, Yosemite National Park,  two seasons of seabird and pinniped monitoring on the Farallon Islands National Wildlife Refuge, diet composition work with California least terns in Baja California, and coordinating [marine debris cleanups on the Channel Islands](https://marinesanctuary.org/goal-clean-seas-channel-islands/).

Currently, I'm a program consultant for Conservation International, working on [Save the Blue 5](https://savethebluefive.net/), a regional initiative focused on climate resilience for marine megafauna. I coordinate research across five countries in Central and South America, working with taxonomic experts, researchers, and climate modelers to assess climate-change vulnerabilities for 11 transboundary species. My work brings together historical literature, species data, and emerging climate modeling to develop science-based products for conservation planning and policy.

I'm first-generation from California, raised on Chumash lands, and currently working on Chumash lands and waters. In my free time I host a weekly radio show on UC Santa Barbara's community radio station KCSB FM called [Chaat Room](https://spinitron.com/KCSB/show/292747/Chaat-Room), highlighting past, present, and future sounds of Cumbia & South Asian beats. I also love to spend time outside and can be found tidepooling, running around with my dog, and surfing point breaks from Devereaux to First Point. In the city you find me dancing to live music.
